newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees "no heightened concern" over Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees "no heightened concern" over Iraq.

text.p: The United States has "no heightened concern" over the situation in Iraq but declines comment on a German newspaper report it is considering a missile strike there, the State Department said on Tuesday.

"There's no change of policy here ... There's no heightened concern in Washington. There's continuing vigilance in Washington on this issue. But I simply can't comment on any prospect of the use of military force," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Burns was responding to questions about an article in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, which said U.N. inspectors had discovered that Iraq has continued to develop missiles in contravention of U.N. resolutions ending the 1991 Gulf War. The newspaper said the United States was contemplating a possible punitive missile strike against Iraq as a result.
Asked whether the United States reserved the right to make such a strike if it deemed this necessary, Burns replied:

"The United States always reserves the right to use its military force to defend its national interest anywhere in the world, but I see no reason to heighten your concern in any way pertaining to the situation in the Middle East."

Burns declined to confirm or deny the report that the Iraqis had maintained a SCUD missile arsenal but said: "There is continuing interest in watching the Iraqis like hawks. No, we do not trust the Iraqis ... The Iraqis don't have the right to be a normal country and develop normal weaponry."
